role.altitude: The cook's week is still the stove, the fridge and the line. Less of it is copying a temperature log, a date list or the day's spend. Whether a batch is safe, whether an ingredient is off, and how the line runs stay with the cook.
reach: Food preparation workers: the same fridge check and the same dated tray, before the food reaches the line
Chefs and head cooks: the weekly kitchen account is a snapshot the cook has already checked, not a new set of books
skills_to_grow: Tell a failed probe from food that is actually outside the safe range
Trust eyes and smell when they disagree with a date label
Refuse to send an account that does not match the till or the deliveries
role.ambitious_version: Before service the cook sees the last good reading on each fridge and oven, which trays are old, and the week's food use against the deliveries. The cook still tastes, still stops a bad batch, and still calls the line.

tasks.short: Storage and cooking temperatures on the line

steps.what: Check stored food is held at the correct temperature.
Keep regulating ovens, broilers, grills and roasters while food is cooked.
Write each stored and cooked temperature into the paper log.
Initial a reading outside the correct temperature range.
Tell the kitchen lead the food is not at the correct temperature.

tasks.design: Probe readings from each fridge and oven land in the {DOCS} hygiene log, and a missed or out-of-range reading raises a notice. The cook still walks the store, still regulates ovens, broilers, grills and roasters, and still initials a reading outside the range. The log does not discard the food.
tasks.previous_blocker: A paper log is written after the round. A dial on the oven does not keep a history the cook can show later.
tasks.enabler_now: A hygiene log can take a probe feed and warn when a measurement is missing. The cook's hands on the equipment are unchanged.
tasks.still_hard: Air in a fridge is not the core of a roast. The cook still probes the food and still decides whether the batch is safe.
tasks.human_edge: The cook feels a door that was left open, smells a fridge that is off, and stops service of that batch before a log says so.

ambition.what: A storage or cooking temperature breach is seen during the service, while the batch can still be held or cooked again.

tasks.altitude: The cook still owns the knobs and the probe. The paper round shrinks to the readings that sit outside the range.

reach.task: Check a fridge temperature at the start of a prep shift
reach.learn: The same probe and the same log apply to a prep fridge. Regulating the ovens, broilers, grills and roasters stays on the line.

evidence.claim: A hygiene-registration app can warn when a temperature measurement is missed and can watch temperatures continuously. That is a log and an alert, not a measurement of cook time saved.
Food-hygiene rules require records commensurate with the nature and size of the business, kept current and available to the authority.
In the Netherlands an approved hygiene code can stand in place of an own plan, and the food authority checks.
An app that logs which member of staff took a reading observes staff. Dutch works-council consent applies. This design stores the appliance and the reading.
Regulating an oven and probing a dish are physical. A log does not do them. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The prior that puts almost all of this task in meetings is the cook standing at a fridge or an oven, not a meeting. The steps treat that time as in person, plus a paper log.

Structured input is a reading with appliance, degrees and time. The producer is the probe, or the cook's own probe when the fixed probe is down. A missing feed is written by hand and is not counted as saved.
Three hours per 100 baseline hours covers false alerts and a failed probe that the cook still writes up. The walk and the regulating are already inside the remaining time of those steps.
No digest case measures minutes saved on temperature logs. Waste-weight cases are not used here.
unknowns: Which fridges and ovens already have a probe the cook trusts.
Whether this site uses an approved hygiene code or its own plan.
Whether the works council already consented to a named hygiene log.
research_questions: On a typical service, how many readings are written by hand, and how many of those are outside the range?

already_counted.description: Walking the cold store and the hot hold, and probing food, stays in the check.
Hands on ovens, broilers, grills and roasters stay in the regulating.
Initialling a real breach, including the decision to hold the batch, stays in the review.

incremental.description: Clear false alerts and write a reading by hand when a probe fails.
The kitchen lead still comes to look when the cook calls a breach.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A service where the cook still writes most readings by hand, because probes cover only the fridges, lands near 4 percent of this task. A service where every fridge and oven already feeds the log, and the cook only initials breaches, lands near 14. Both sit under the central net, because regulating the equipment and probing the food stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check freshness and quality of ingredients by sight and smell.
Keep rotating stock so older items are used first.
Keep track of old and new items on date labels.
Decide that ingredient quality has failed and discard it.
Tell the buyer which stock items are running short.

tasks.design: Goods-in dates land on a stock list in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, so old and new items are visible without recopying labels into a book. The cook still checks freshness and quality by sight and smell, still rotates stock, and still discards what has failed. The list does not declare food fresh.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dates live on tape and in one person's head. A list on paper is recopied and drifts from the shelf.
tasks.enabler_now: A stock record can take the delivery date and the open date and sort the oldest items first. Looking at the food is unchanged.
tasks.still_hard: A date can be right while the fish smells wrong. The cook still decides the discard.
tasks.human_edge: The cook sees slime, frost damage or a broken seal that a date label will not show.
tasks.altitude: The cook still owns freshness. The list only stops the recopying of dates.

reach.task: Rotate stock in the prep store and flag a pack that looks off
reach.learn: The same date list helps a prep shift. The line cook's decision to discard during service does not move to the list.

evidence.claim: Freshness of ingredients is judged by sight, smell and date, and rotating stock is physical work. A list of dates does not replace either. Model knowledge.
A weighed and identified discard can feed a food-use record. That is a record of what was thrown away, not a judgement that food was fresh.

assumptions: The prior that puts most of this task in meetings is the cook at the shelf, not a meeting. The steps treat the check and the rotation as in person, and the date list as a document.

Structured input is item, received date, open date and location. The producer is goods-in, or the cook when a pack arrives without a date. The fallback is a handwritten label, and that writing stays in the remaining time.
Three hours per 100 baseline hours covers labels that will not scan and a list the cook corrects after a delivery. Looking and rotating are already inside the remaining time.
The waste-weight cases in the digest are kilograms, not minutes on this task, so they are not used as a time result.
unknowns: Whether goods-in already records a date the kitchen can see, or only the buyer can.
Who is allowed to discard expensive items without a second look.
research_questions: What share of packs arrive with a usable date, and what share does the cook still label by hand?

already_counted.description: Sight and smell checks stay in the freshness step.
Correcting a date the list got wrong stays in the label review.
The decision to discard stays in full.

incremental.description: Fix labels that will not scan and correct the list after a mixed delivery.
The buyer still turns a shortage note into an order.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week of handwritten labels and a paper list the cook still recopies lands near 4 percent of this task. A week where goods-in dates already feed the list, and the cook only corrects clashes, lands near 12. Both sit under the central net, because the eye, the nose and the rotation stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise the kitchen line through service

steps.what: Read the booking list before you coordinate kitchen staff.
Supervise kitchen staff through service on the line.
Correct dish timing while the kitchen line is in service.
Answer a cook who asks how the station work should go.
Note the next service station change for kitchen staff.

tasks.design: A service sheet in {DOCS} is filled from the booking count and the menu before the line starts, so the cook is not rewriting the same stations by hand. During service the cook still supervises kitchen staff, still corrects timing, and still answers a question in person. The sheet does not score anyone.
tasks.previous_blocker: The booking count sits on a scrap or in a verbal briefing, and the same stations are rewritten each day.
tasks.enabler_now: A sheet can be filled from the booking count and the house menu with ordinary fields. Calling the line cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A full dining room and a late table are a live judgement. The sheet does not hear the pass.
tasks.human_edge: The cook sees who is behind, who is free, and when to hold a course. That look is the supervision.
tasks.altitude: The cook still runs the line. The only shrink is rewriting the booking sheet and the next-day station note.

reach.task: Set stations for a prep shift from the same booking count
reach.learn: The service sheet can be read by a prep supervisor. The live call during restaurant service stays with the cook.

evidence.claim: Assigning stations and correcting timing during service are in-person supervision. A prepared sheet does not do them. Model knowledge.
Annex III, as cited, does not cover a station list built from bookings and a menu. This design does not score cooks or rank who was slow.
A log of who did what on the line would observe staff and needs Dutch works-council consent. This design does not keep that log.

assumptions: The prior that puts most of this task in meetings is the cook on the line talking to staff, not a scheduled meeting. The steps treat service as in person.

Structured input is covers by time and the menu sections on for that service. The producer is the booking list. If the list is a phone note, the cook still types the count, and that typing stays in the remaining time of the sheet step.
Two hours per 100 baseline hours covers a wrong booking count the cook fixes on the sheet. Supervision during service is already inside the remaining time.
Nothing in the digest measures minutes saved on kitchen supervision.
unknowns: Whether the booking count is already a field the kitchen can read, or a number shouted by the front of house.
Whether a station note kept by name would be treated as a staff record under national rules.
research_questions: How often is the booking count wrong at the start of service, and who corrects it?

already_counted.description: Reading the filled sheet and fixing a wrong cover count stays in the review.
Writing the next service station change stays in that note.

incremental.description: Correct a booking count that arrived late or changed after the sheet was filled.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A service where the booking count arrives as a scrap and the cook still builds the sheet by hand lands near 2 percent of this task. A service where the count and the menu already fill the sheet, and the cook only reads it, lands near 8. Both sit under the central net, because supervising the line and correcting timing stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Kitchen records and the weekly account

steps.what: Collect till totals and delivery notes for the kitchen records.
Post point-of-sale till totals into the kitchen accounts.
Read a handwritten delivery note into the kitchen accounts.

loop.purpose: Read item, quantity and unit price off a handwritten delivery note into account lines.
loop.input: A photo or scan of one handwritten delivery note.
loop.output: Lines with supplier, item name, quantity and unit price.
loop.check: Each line's item name, quantity and unit price match the note, not only a supplier code.
loop.stop: Stop after one pass, or when a line has no quantity.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed column map cannot read a handwritten note whose layout changes by supplier.

steps.what: Check a kitchen record that clashes with the till total.
Send the accepted weekly kitchen accounts to the finance team.

tasks.design: Till totals from the {OTHER} point-of-sale post into the kitchen account in the {ERP}, and a handwritten delivery note is read once into the same lines. The cook checks any clash with the till or the note, and that checked snapshot is the only version that can be sent to finance. Configure the {ERP} posting before any custom code.
tasks.previous_blocker: The cook retypes till slips and delivery notes into a sheet, and a mismatch shows up when finance asks.
tasks.enabler_now: Till totals and electronic delivery totals can post on a schedule. A bounded read covers the notes that are still handwritten. The cook still attests the week.
tasks.still_hard: A supplier's note that does not match the goods, and a till total the cook does not recognise, still need a person. Finance still posts the ledger.
tasks.human_edge: The cook knows which delivery was short and which waste note was a spilled pot, and will not send a week that hides either.

ambition.what: Food use against the week's deliveries is visible before the account is sent, every week rather than when finance asks.

tasks.altitude: The cook still attests the week and still decides a clash. The retyping of till totals and clean delivery notes goes away.

reach.task: Read the weekly kitchen account before planning the next menu's cost
reach.learn: The same snapshot shows food use against deliveries. Pricing the menu and talking to finance about the ledger stay with the chef.

evidence.claim: A recipe record can hold supplier prices so a food cost follows a price change. That supports the kitchen account of food cost, not the statutory books.
A hygiene-registration app can store measurements and warn when one is missed. That covers the hygiene-log part of kitchen records, not the spend account.
A discard can be weighed and identified into a food-use record. The published waste-weight figures are kilograms, not minutes of cook time, and are not used as a time result.
Hygiene records must be kept current and shown to the authority, commensurate with the size of the business.
Annex III, as cited, does not cover food records or a kitchen account. This design does not score staff.
No source in the digest measures time saved on costing or on keeping kitchen accounts. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The prior that puts about half of this task in meetings overstates the case. The work is delivery notes, a till slip and a spreadsheet, plus a short send to finance.

On an ordinary week the cook attests the snapshot they just checked. A second person is not today's practice, so no head-cook share is invented. If the company later wants a second signature, that time is extra.

Structured input is till gross and cover count from the point-of-sale export, and supplier, item, quantity and unit price from an electronic delivery message. The producer is the till and the supplier. A handwritten note uses the bounded read, and the cook's clash check is the fallback.

Test the finance system's own posting before custom code. Seven hours per 100 baseline hours covers failed imports and notes the read got wrong. Finance's ledger posting is their work and is not taken out of the cook's saving.
The invoice-speed and waste-kilogram stories in the digest are not used as a time result for this task.
unknowns: Whether the till can export a daily total the kitchen is allowed to read.
What share of delivery notes is still handwritten.
Whether finance will accept the kitchen snapshot as the source for food cost, or will rekey it.
research_questions: In a normal week, how many delivery notes are electronic, how many are handwritten, and how many clash with the goods or the till?

already_counted.description: Chasing the paper notes that did not arrive electronically stays in the collect step.
Checking a clash and attesting that snapshot stays in the review.
Sending the attested snapshot, and answering one question about it, stays in the send.

incremental.description: Repair a failed till import and correct a handwritten note the read got wrong.
Finance still posts the ledger and asks when the snapshot is short.

approvals.approved_version: Weekly kitchen account snapshot with till totals, delivery lines and the waste note, as checked by the cook

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week of handwritten delivery notes, where the cook still gathers paper and checks many clashes, lands near 22 percent of this task. A week where the till and the suppliers already post totals, and only a couple of notes are read, lands near 48. Both sit under the central net. Finance's ledger work is outside this saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
